_meta.indication: ZALTRAP, in combination with 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, irinotecan (FOLFIRI), is indicated for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) that is resistant to or has progressed following an oxaliplatin-containing regimen

pivotal_trials.design: Single, multinational, randomized (1:1), placebo-controlled, double-blind trial; patients received ziv-aflibercept 4 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks or matching placebo in combination with FOLFIRI; randomization stratified by ECOG status and prior bevacizumab therapy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients age ≥ 18 years with histologically/cytologically documented adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, who progressed during or following a maximum of one prior oxaliplatin-containing regimen (or relapsed within 6 months of oxaliplatin-containing adjuvant therapy); no prior irinotecan
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) by independent radiologic review using RECIST v1.0; key secondary endpoint overall response rate (ORR)
pivotal_trials.result: OS: median 13.50 vs 12.06 months (ZALTRAP/FOLFIRI vs placebo/FOLFIRI), stratified HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.71 to 0.94), log-rank p=0.0032. PFS: median 6.9 vs 4.7 months, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.66 to 0.87), p=0.00007. ORR: 19.8% vs 11.1%, p=0.0001.

nct_ctgov.title: Aflibercept Versus Placebo in Combination With Irinotecan and 5-FU in the Treatment of Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer After Failure of an Oxaliplatin Based Regimen

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (all grades, ≥20% incidence and at least 2% greater incidence for the ZALTRAP/FOLFIRI regimen) were leukopenia (78% vs 72%), diarrhea (69% vs 57%), neutropenia (67% vs 57%), proteinuria (62% vs 41%), AST increased (62% vs 54%), stomatitis (50% vs 33%), fatigue (48% vs 39%), thrombocytopenia (48% vs 35%), ALT increased (50% vs 39%), hypertension (41% vs 11%). Boxed-warning risks: Grade 3-4 hemorrhagic events (3% vs 1%) and Grade 3-4 GI perforation, plus Grade 3 compromised wound healing; bleeding/hemorrhage (all grades) in 38% vs 19%.
target_moa: Ziv-aflibercept is a recombinant fusion protein (VEGF-binding portions of VEGF Receptors 1 and 2 fused to the Fc of human IgG1) that acts as a soluble decoy receptor binding VEGF-A, VEGF-B, and PlGF, inhibiting activation of their cognate receptors and thereby inhibiting angiogenesis
modality: Recombinant fusion protein (soluble decoy receptor; other)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HEMORRHAGE, GASTROINTESTINAL PERFORATION, COMPROMISED WOUND HEALING — severe and sometimes fatal hemorrhage including GI hemorrhage; GI perforation including fatal; severe compromised wound healing

rems.type: A REMS is not required to ensure safe use of ziv-aflibercept

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use and Pharmacokinetics labeling with data from pediatric trial COG-AVDL0714 (did not add a new indication)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides updates to the USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS, Pediatric Use (8.4) and CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, Pharmacokinetics (12.3) subsections of the package insert to include data from pediatric trial COG-AVDL0714, entitled "Aflibercept in Treating Young Patients with Relapsed or Refractory Solid Tumors."

summary.text: Traditional (full) approval based on substantial evidence of effectiveness from the single randomized, placebo-controlled VELOUR trial demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival; the application was not referred to an advisory committee and a REMS was not required.

citations.quote: The application provides substantial evidence of efficacy on an important endpoint (survival) and demonstrated in an adequate safety database that the toxicity profile is acceptable and qualitatively similar to that observed with the other approved anti-angiogenic biologic product, bevacizumab (i.e., there are no novel or unusual safety signals).
This application was not referred to an advisory committee.
